# HarnessDock v0.1.5-rc.3

HarnessDock `v0.1.5-rc.3` is a release-candidate rebuild of the current `0.1.5` client line after CI/release-pipeline hardening. It keeps the same verified DeepSeek Harness Runtime source as rc.2 and does not change the sealed Runtime identity, RuntimeLease, WebView trust boundary, startup policy or Windows NSIS-only packaging contract.

## Runtime provenance

- Upstream source remains `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2`.
- Upstream commit remains `fb2c4b9e698e30edb738bca4cf0618587db7d203`.
- Desktop targets continue to package the exact sealed local Runtime derived from that source.
- Android and iOS remain Remote Gateway clients and do not embed a desktop Runtime.

The HarnessDock client prerelease advances independently to `rc.3`; no nonexistent upstream `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.3` package or tag is invented.

## Build and CI hardening

- Added one repository-local `setup-tauri-cli` action for candidate and Tauri CI jobs.
- The action reads the exact Tauri CLI version from the repository version SSOT, builds it with `cargo install --locked --force --root` on cache miss, and verifies the exact binary version on both cache hits and misses.
- Tauri CLI cache identity is scoped by operating system, architecture, Rust toolchain and exact Tauri CLI version, with no broad restore key.
- Android, iOS, Windows, Linux and macOS candidate jobs now use the same exact CLI setup path instead of duplicating installation logic.
- The clean one-click build path remains independent and continues deleting local bootstrap/tool state, so clean-clone evidence cannot be hidden by the candidate cache.
- `check:versions` now treats raw workflow Tauri CLI installs, Rust/Tauri version pin drift, missing trigger paths and setup-action provenance drift as hard failures.
- Rust continues to use `rust-toolchain.toml` as its SSOT; Tauri CLI continues to use `scripts/versions.json` as its SSOT.

## Release-pipeline hardening

- Automatic post-release maintenance no longer manufactures a publish failure merely because an already-published historical prerelease tag points to an older SHA.
- The automated workflow verifies the existing managed prerelease and can explicitly skip a duplicate publication attempt when appropriate.
- Manual publication and invalid/unmanaged tag reuse remain strict failures.
- Same-SHA CI, Windows packaged-startup, candidate asset verification, checksum verification and Runtime provenance checks are unchanged and remain mandatory for this new `v0.1.5-rc.3` tag.

## Release scope

This candidate carries forward the rc.2 startup/profile and managed-process lifecycle hardening, including direct Harness Web startup, profile-aware Runtime launch preferences, scoped plugin quarantine, Windows Job Object containment, Unix process-group cleanup and no-orphan shutdown verification.

`v0.1.5-rc.3` is published as a GitHub prerelease. Stable releases remain subject to the stable signing/update-manifest policy.
